diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\mathcal G=\left\{ \mathbf U : z_1\rho_1 > 0, z_2\rho_2 > 0, \ c^2(\mathbf U)>0,\ z_1\in[0,1] \right\}$

issues.failure_explanation: The counterexample claims $\mathbf{U}^{(1)}$ and $\mathbf{U}^{(2)}$ belong to $\mathcal{G}$, but $\mathbf{U}^{(1)}$ has second component $z_2\rho_2=0$ and $\mathbf{U}^{(2)}$ has first component $z_1\rho_1=0$. The definition of $\mathcal{G}$ requires both partial densities to be strictly positive, so neither state is in $\mathcal{G}$. Thus the convex combination of these two states does not demonstrate non-convexity of $\mathcal{G}$.

failure_location.quote: Step 1: Verification of state $\mathbf{U}^{(1)} \in \mathcal{G}$, For state 1, it represents pure phase 1 ($z_1 = 1$, $\rho_1 = 1.2$).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Modify the two states to have both partial densities strictly positive (e.g., add a small amount of the missing phase) and re-verify that they lie in $\mathcal{G}$, or remove the counterexample.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix's claim that $\mathcal{G}$ is non-convex is not supported by the provided counterexample.
issues.title: Appendix A counterexample uses states outside the admissible set G
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local adjustment of the counterexample; the main convexity theorem for $\mathcal{G}^p$ is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp}

issues.failure_explanation: The piecewise definition of $\theta_{z_1}$ uses the first branch whenever $m_{i,j} < \varepsilon_z$, even if also $M_{i,j} > 1-\varepsilon_z$. In that case it enforces only the lower bound and may still leave $z_1 > 1-\varepsilon_z$ at the point where the maximum is attained. The standard limiter requires taking the minimum of the two scaling factors when both bounds are violated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the piecewise formula with $\theta_{z_1} = \min\{ (\overline{z}_1-\varepsilon_z)/(\overline{z}_1-m),\ (1-\varepsilon_z-\overline{z}_1)/(M-\overline{z}_1) \}$ whenever either bound is violated.
issues.overall_effect: The BP limiter does not guarantee the upper volume-fraction bound $z_1 \le 1-\varepsilon_z$ in all cases, so the claim that the limiter enforces $\mathbf{U} \in \mathcal{G}^p$ is not fully established.
issues.title: Volume-fraction BP limiter omits the minimum of lower and upper bound constraints
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line correction to a limiter formula and preserves the intended BP guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathcal G^p=\left\{ \mathbf U : z_1\rho_1 > 0, z_2\rho_2 > 0, \ p(\mathbf U)>0,\ z_1\in[0,1] \right\}
The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp}

issues.failure_explanation: The formula for $\theta_p$ assumes that the pressure along the segment from $\overline{\mathbf{U}}$ to $\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}$ is linear (or at least concave), so that setting the linear interpolation to $\varepsilon_p$ ensures the actual pressure is $\ge \varepsilon_p$. For the Tammann EOS the pressure is not concave in the conserved variables. A concrete counterexample: take $\rho_1=\rho_2=1$, $\gamma_1=1.4$, $p_{w,1}=0$, $\gamma_2=4.4$, $p_{w,2}=6000$, $\overline{\mathbf{U}}=(0.01,0.99,0,20000,0.01)$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}=(0.99,0.01,0,0,0.99)$. Then $p(\overline{\mathbf{U}})\approx 38940$, $p(\widetilde{\mathbf{U}})\approx -31.33$, $\theta_p\approx 0.9992$, and the limited state has $p\approx -27.4<0$. Thus the limiter can fail to enforce pressure positivity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pressure limiter with a correct projection onto $\mathcal{G}^p$, e.g., find the largest $\theta\in[0,1]$ such that $p(\overline{\mathbf{U}}+\theta(\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}-\overline{\mathbf{U}}))\ge \varepsilon_p$ by solving the scalar equation $p(\theta)=\varepsilon_p$ (e.g., via bisection using the convexity of $\mathcal{G}^p$).
issues.overall_effect: The BP limiter does not guarantee $p>0$, so the claimed unconditional BP property of the full BP-OEDG scheme for pressure is not established.
issues.title: Pressure BP limiter does not guarantee pressure positivity for Tammann EOS
issues.why_classification: The central BP guarantee for pressure is lost without a new limiter and proof; the repair requires a nontrivial algorithmic change and revalidation of the BP property.
